      "startEvent": 1635,
      "endEvent": 1638,
      "contextStartEvent": 1597,
      "contextEndEvent": 1677,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "the thing about a pattern is that it's a pattern.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Asked for a Christian pattern no longer applicable (E1629–E1632), Pageau substitutes a tautology for explaining why being a pattern ensures continued applicability. His ensuing account supplies hierarchy and love, but no such guarantee. Distinguishing applications from patterns (E1665–E1674) might insulate the claim, though it also permits substantive disagreement over applications."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1963,
      "endEvent": 1975,
      "contextStartEvent": 1900,
      "contextEndEvent": 1994,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "the solution to making Christianity better is to be a Christian and to make it better.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The insider requirement discounts external criticism by the critic's position rather than its merits (E1966–E1975). Embodied dependence on stories supplies an argument (E1958–E1962), but does not establish why outsiders cannot identify errors. Uncertainty concerns whether the compact affirmation substitutes for that missing bridge or summarizes an incomplete ordinary argument; he also requests explicit evaluative goals."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1985,
      "endEvent": 1988,
      "contextStartEvent": 1900,
      "contextEndEvent": 1994,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "Because no ideology is bug-free.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The universal maxim supplies a reason for rejecting Christianity's presumed freedom from error, without establishing that every ideology contains errors. However, Woodford has offered specific historical counterexamples and conflicting prescriptions (E1900–E1938), and immediately qualifies Christianity's fallibility as very likely (E1987). This may summarize his broader case rather than replace it."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2124,
      "endEvent": 2134,
      "contextStartEvent": 2060,
      "contextEndEvent": 2150,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "But that has to be done from within in life.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Following another reply, Pageau renews the requirement that reform originate inside the tradition, comparing it to citizenship (E2130–E2134). This restricts critics' standing independently of particular evidence. It is an argued procedural restriction, not a slogan replacing reasons. He explicitly accepts outdated Christian practices (E2119–E2124) and questions the proposed external standard, limiting the protection's scope."
    }
  ],
